title: Keep high-cardinality identifiers out of metric labels

facts.note: Any metric item of a telemetry tracking plan, whatever its file name or location; recognised by the item's signal kind (metric) and its dimensions list, not by a filename pattern. Applies equally to new, edited and existing items.

values: metric dimension with missing or high cardinality
metric dimension naming a property declared cardinality high
facts.note: Optional corroboration only: available only when the planner_telemetry_plan validator has actually been run or its output inspected. Absence of a reported finding is not a precondition; the rule applies to the metric item regardless.

fires: A metric item lists a dimension declared cardinality high.
A metric item lists a dimension with no declared cardinality.
A metric dimension is named after a property (e.g. a request/user/session id) that the item declares cardinality high.
An existing metric item is reviewed or validated and one of its dimensions violates the above, even though nobody is editing it.
doesNotFire: An event, log or trace item declares a property with cardinality high, justified by the plan.
A metric item whose dimensions all declare low or medium cardinality and name no high-cardinality property.

given: A telemetry tracking plan contains a metric item (new, edited or existing).
when: You declare or review the metric's dimensions (labels).
then: Every dimension declares a cardinality of low or medium; none is declared high and none names a property the item declares cardinality high.
prefer: Keep the identifier, change the signal: label the metric with bounded dimensions (e.g. an outcome, cardinality low) and carry the identifier as an event, log or trace property declared cardinality high — for example on the sibling event's properties. If the identifier is already carried by such a property, removing it from the metric dimensions is enough.

Treat any property whose distinct-value volume is unbounded or near-unbounded (request ids, user ids, session tokens) as a high-cardinality identifier and carry it as an event, log or trace property, where cardinality is the point rather than a liability.
To check a dimension, compare its name with the item's declared properties; if a property of that name is declared cardinality high, the dimension is rejected.
avoid: Dropping the identifier from the plan entirely instead of carrying it as an event/log/trace property.
Leaving a metric dimension's cardinality undeclared, or relabelling a high-cardinality id as low/medium to pass the check.
unless: Event, log and trace properties may declare cardinality high where justified; this rule judges metric dimensions only.
why: Every distinct metric-label value becomes a new time series, so a high-cardinality label is a backend outage with a YAML file attached; the plan is where that mistake is cheapest to catch.
evidence: When the planner_telemetry_plan validator has been run, it reports no finding for the metric item.
Each entry in the metric item's dimensions list has a name and cardinality in {low, medium}.

Each high-cardinality identifier removed from metric dimensions is still carried in the plan as an event, log or trace property (declared cardinality high where justified); a sibling event is one acceptable placement, not a requirement.
verifier_detail: Dimension = an entry of the metric item's dimensions list, with a name and a declared cardinality (low, medium or high).
High-cardinality identifier = a property whose distinct-value volume is unbounded or near-unbounded (request ids, user ids, session tokens).
Reject when: dimension cardinality missing; dimension cardinality == high; or dimension name matches a property the item declares cardinality high.
Scope: all metric items regardless of file name; event, log and trace properties with cardinality high are legal and not judged.

Source fix example (illustrative): # telemetry/commons/response-invocation-accepted/metric.be.duration.json  "dimensions": [{ "name": "outcome", "cardinality": "low" }]  # response_id moves to the sibling event's properties, declared cardinality high.
audit: Source name: High-cardinality identifiers are forbidden as metric labels

sharedNodes.text: strict: atdd-bun fails on every finding; it has no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.

additions.text: Relabelling a high-cardinality id as low/medium to pass the check; dropping the identifier from the plan entirely.
additions.justification: Metric-gaming/anti-pattern framing of the source's 'the identifier still belongs in the plan' and declared-cardinality requirement; required by the authoring instructions.
Required structure; derived directly from the statement, normative text and exception.

additions.text: prefer[2]: compare a dimension's name with the item's declared properties to find whether it names a high-cardinality property; prefer[0] clause 'if already carried by such a property, removing it from metric dimensions is enough'.
additions.justification: Operational restatement of S015 and S016 to address reviewer usability risks; adds no new obligation (the sibling event stays illustrative).
